s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown plaque with ecchymosis in the axilla
salient_findings: Asymptomatic, reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
key_facts: 5-year history of gradually enlarging plaque
No previous history of trauma
No systemic symptoms
Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm plaque
No local lymphadenopathy
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests were negative

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, reddish-brown plaque with ecchymosis

shortlist.label: Verrucous hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similarities with the case's clinical and histological findings, including vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40

shortlist.label: Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of hemosiderin deposits and the lesion's appearance

shortlist.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the histologic findings of vascular spaces lined with a single layer of bland endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely due to negative HHV-8 serology, it remains a consideration given the clinical presentation and vascular proliferation

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border and the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation with hemosiderin deposits are consistent with targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.

rejected.label: Verrucous hemangioma
rejected.why: Verrucous hemangioma typically presents with a more verrucous surface and is not as commonly associated with the distinctive hemosiderotic features seen in this case.

rejected.label: Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous lesion
rejected.why: This lesion does not typically present as a large, well-defined plaque and lacks the specific vascular features described.

rejected.label: Spindle cell hemangioma
rejected.why: Spindle cell hemangioma is characterized by a distinct spindle cell component and cavernous vascular spaces, which were not described in this case.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Kaposi's sarcoma is typically associated with HHV-8 positivity, which was negative in this case, and often presents in the context of immunosuppression or with more systemic symptoms.
